title: Finocchi al Forno
subtitle: Baked fennel with parmesan and olive oil
excerpt: Finocchi al forno is halved fennel bulbs baked in olive oil until soft and caramelised, then scattered with parmesan and returned to the oven until golden and bubbling. The fennel loses its raw anise edge and becomes sweet and tender. It works as a side dish or a light vegetarian main.
sourceNotes: Baked fennel with parmesan is a standard of Italian home cooking, particularly associated with Rome and central Italy, where fennel is cultivated widely. The dish appears in several regional Italian cookbooks and is a common oven-baked vegetable preparation across the country.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake up to the parmesan stage, cool, and refrigerate. Add parmesan and finish in the oven 15 minutes before serving.

content.text: Baked fennel is one of the quieter Italian vegetable preparations: the raw anise flavour mellows completely in the oven and turns sweet and almost buttery. The fennel bulbs are halved, drizzled with olive oil, and baked until caramelised at the edges, then scattered with parmesan and returned to the oven for 15 more minutes. The parmesan browns and crisps on top while the fennel underneath stays soft. It is a side dish that can hold its own against a main course.

items.prepNote: outer leaves removed, halved lengthways through the core

content.text: Heat the oven to 190°C. Arrange the fennel halves cut-side up in a baking dish that holds them snugly.
Drizzle with the olive oil and season with salt and black pepper. Add 4 tablespoons of water to the dish.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for 30 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for a further 10 minutes until the fennel is tender and the cut surfaces are beginning to colour.
Scatter the grated parmesan over the fennel halves. Return to the oven for 12 to 15 minutes until the cheese is golden and bubbling. Serve hot from the dish.

Fennel is particularly beloved in Roman and central Italian cooking. Rome has a tradition of raw fennel served at the end of a meal to aid digestion. Baked fennel with parmesan is the cooked counterpart: a simple oven side dish that turns a strong-flavoured raw vegetable into something mild, sweet, and rich. It pairs well with pork, fish, and poultry.
